$comment: Mainnet object IDs the fork sandbox references (DBSF-016). The fork inherits mainnet state, so these are MAINNET identities — not localnet deploys. Verified live against mainnet gRPC on the date below; re-verify with `pnpm verify:deepbook-ids` (from sandbox/devstack-plugins), which also detects packages upgraded past their pin (listPackageVersions). `originalId` is forever and is what type tags are stamped with; `latestId` (a new id per upgrade) is the moveCall target. Pool tickSize/lotSize/minSize were originally captured from the deepbook indexer and drifted (SUI_USDC tickSize was 100 vs the chain's 10, which the Trading page's order validation would have enforced against users); all nine values were re-read from the chain on 2026-08-13 and now match. `pnpm verify:deepbook-ids` does NOT cover them — they live in the pool's PoolInner dynamic field (pool -> Versioned inner df -> allowed_versions/pool_id, then book.tick_size/lot_size/min_size), so re-verify by reading that field. Note: @mysten/deepbook-v3 1.5.0's mainnetPackageIds lags mainnet for margin (pins v5, mainnet is v6) — trust the verify script over the SDK constants.

pyth.$comment: Pyth/Wormhole identities for the oracle loop (SEDEFI-317 / DBSF-013). The package ids here were verified CURRENT at the fork pin — wormhole has never been upgraded (UpgradeCap version 1, latest == original) and pyth is at version 2 — so an `assert_version` abort is NOT package skew. It is SUI-FORK-ISSUES #2: `wormhole::vaa::parse_and_verify` and `package_utils::assert_version` read CHILD objects, which the fork's execution path never lazy-fetches. Every id under `prewarm` must be read once by id (a plain gRPC getObject materializes it) before the first update PTB of a fresh chain, or the update aborts. Re-derive them by enumerating the State objects' dynamic fields against MAINNET (the fork's dynamic_field_iter is a patched-out todo!() stub and returns empty); ids are parent+key derived, so they are identical on the fork.
